evidence.bullet: EAL covers learners exposed to a language other than English in early development or at home
evidence.quote: In Guernsey, English as an Additional Language (EAL) applies to learners who have been exposed to a language other than English in early development, or continue to be in their home environment, regardless of their proficiency in English

evidence.bullet: A learner is EAL whatever their English proficiency, including locally born bilinguals
evidence.quote: they may be locally born children growing up in bilingual households, or learners who have recently arrived in Guernsey from another country

evidence.bullet: Where two languages were present early, the non-English one is noted as first language
evidence.quote: when more than one language was present in early development, the non-English language should be noted as the learner's first language

evidence.bullet: EAL Service support is intended for those with some difficulty accessing the curriculum
evidence.quote: Support from the EAL Service is intended for those who have some difficulty accessing the curriculum because of low proficiency in English

evidence.bullet: A child joining after the first term of Year 10 is placed by an experienced Education Officer
evidence.quote: Children will be allocated a place at the most appropriate school based on their current school's curriculum and their chosen examination subject options; this being determined by an experienced Education Officer

sources.label: English as an Additional Language, States of Guernsey, Education Inclusion Services
